claims.text: Nitriding high-entropy alloy fasteners will create a nitride-enriched surface layer.
Nitriding will improve the mechanical durability of high-entropy alloy fasteners relative to untreated fasteners.
Nitriding will reduce room-temperature creep in high-entropy alloy fasteners relative to untreated fasteners.
Nitriding will improve the corrosion resistance of high-entropy alloy fasteners relative to untreated fasteners.
Suitable plasma or gas nitriding conditions can promote nitrogen uptake without degrading the bulk microstructure.
The nitrided surface layer will contain fine nitride precipitates and/or nitrogen in solid solution.
The nitride-enriched surface layer will introduce compressive residual stresses.
The formed nitride layer will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will improve mechanical durability.
Impeded dislocation motion will improve room-temperature creep resistance.
The nitride layer will act as a barrier to corrosive species.
The barrier effect of the nitride layer will enhance corrosion resistance.
Nitrided samples will exhibit moderately improved yield strength relative to untreated samples.
Nitrided samples will exhibit lower room-temperature creep strain relative to untreated samples.
Nitrided samples will exhibit a measurably lower corrosion rate relative to untreated samples.
The proposed benefits depend on nitriding parameters that produce sufficient nitride formation without undesirable phase changes or microstructural damage.
The treatment will be most effective for high-entropy alloys whose compositions permit appreciable nitrogen uptake and diffusion.
